extracted.intended_audience: writers, playwrights, and literature students studying use of humor in serious works
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for inserting and evaluating comedic moments within otherwise serious or tragic literary works, focusing on timing, character consistency, and how humor interacts with dramatic tension. Includes a short evaluative rubric and descriptive categories/types of comic relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serves the larger work (does not derail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comic moment serve the larger work (not derail it)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comic moment should contribute to the overall piece rather than taking attention away from the main narrative or undermining major themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the timing appropriate (in a tense moment)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place comic moments strategically, often in or around tension to allow relief without undercutting stakes; timing affects whether the laugh refreshes the audience or distracts them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Releases tension without negating it
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it release tension without negating it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The humor should allow emotional recharge while preserving the seriousness of the surrounding material so subsequent tragic moments remain impactful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character consistency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic moments must align with established character traits; a joke should feel believable for the character delivering it and not break characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deepens rather than flattens contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it deepen rather than flatten the contrast?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good comic relief heightens the contrast between humor and seriousness, making both poles more potent instead of reducing their dramatic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relieves tension and allows emotional recharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Relieves Tension — Reduces tension in-story for characters and real-world for audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions: reduces in-story tension, allows audience to recharge emotionally, and can make subsequent tragic moments more impactful by providing a reset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supports character development
rubrics_metrics.description: Character Development — Comic relief can develop character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic relief characters are set apart by their humor; a serious character with a comic moment shows another side and humor can humanize high-stakes figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heightens dramatic effect via contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Heightens Dramatic Effect — Contrasting humor with seriousness emphasizes gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone shifts created by comic relief emphasize both the comedic and tragic elements, making dramatic moments feel weightier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-driven comic relief
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor arises from a character's personality, traits, or behavior; the character themselves provide the comic element rather than the situation or dialogue alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation-based comic relief
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor emerges from the circumstances or events unfolding in the plot rather than from a character's quirks or explicit jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical (slapstick) comic relief
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical comedy—visual or bodily actions—used to produce laughter; best used when it doesn't break the story's tone or stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogic (witty banter) comic relief
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor delivered through dialogue—repartee, quips, or witty exchanges—that can reveal character and relieve tension without disrupting plot flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony-based comic relief
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor rooted in situational or verbal irony; can underscore themes and highlight contrasts between expectation and reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical or parodic comic relief
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor that parodies or satirizes elements within or outside the work; useful for commentary but must be balanced so it doesn't undermine the serious thread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal vs. external comic relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal vs. External — whether characters in the story laugh too or only the audience laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal comic relief: characters react and laugh within the story world; External comic relief: only the audience is meant to laugh and characters do not acknowledge the humor. Choice affects tone and audience engagement.
